A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same robustness-scaling study. The main text and Appendices A–H are available, including readable tables, figures, algorithms, and equations. Reformatting and renumbering do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original Pythia and Qwen2.5 experiments measuring clean accuracy, attack success, adversarial-training efficiency, robustness transfer, and perplexity-filter behavior.

after.justification: V5 retains these original experiments and reports additional Qwen2.5 accuracy and attack-success results on IMDB and Helpful.

M1.justification: The classifier adaptation, GCG and BEAST implementations, RandomToken attack, and adversarial-training procedure are unchanged. The 200 new attacked examples and 1,000 training examples per round now described in Section 5 were already specified in v4 Appendix D.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six classification tasks and StrongREJECT generation task. The added Qwen2.5 experiments concern IMDB and Helpful, which were already evaluated with Pythia; they expand model/task configurations without introducing different datasets, task requirements, or threat scenarios.

E2.justification: GCG, RandomToken, and BEAST remain the evaluated attack methods, with the same adversarial-training and transfer comparisons. The BEAST panels added to main-text Figure 3 represent comparisons already present in v4 Appendix C.5.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation expands to Qwen2.5 on the existing IMDB and Helpful tasks, adding model/task configurations in Table 1 and Figure 2. The stated metrics, preprocessing, training budgets, attack strengths, and adversarial-training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing suffix-to-infix robustness-transfer analysis has revised Pythia/Spam curves in v5 Figure 7 versus v4 Figure 6, changing its supporting evidence while retaining the larger-model transfer conclusion. The other threat-model, attack-transfer, and perplexity-filter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification medians and min–max ranges over at least three seeds, 95% Wilson intervals for StrongREJECT, and one seed for the prefix attack. Some plotted values and bands change, but no change in run counts or uncertainty-reporting procedures is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces Qwen2.5 dashes with IMDB accuracies of 0.950/0.965 and Helpful accuracies of 0.670/0.710 for 0.5B/14B models. Figures 2 and 8 add corresponding attack-success and clean-accuracy curves. Existing Pythia/Spam adversarial-training and infix-transfer curves also change. These are added or revised results, with the broad scaling conclusions retained.

T1.justification: The logit–compute derivation in Appendix C.5.1, adversarial-sampling equations in Appendix D.2, compute approximations in Appendix E, and interpolation procedure in Appendix G are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The central findings about model size, attack scaling, adversarial-training efficiency and transfer, and the conditional long-run defender advantage remain. V5 foregrounds the scaling framework and classification/safety-training scope, but these contributions and boundaries were already present in v4.

C2.justification: V5 explicitly links the StrongREJECT size trend to larger models' safety-training sample efficiency and removes v4's specific conjecture that distillation explains robustness differences between easy and hard Qwen2.5 tasks. It also flags a RandomToken compute-axis error in Figure 23. Section 7's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V5 adds a project-code repository link in the abstract and discloses that the two smallest-model curves in the RandomToken clean-accuracy plot are incorrectly shifted right. The training-pool quantities newly repeated in Section 5 were already documented in v4 Appendix D.2 and do not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: V5 adds Wang et al. (2023) on adversarial attacks against superhuman Go systems and removes the Jain et al. (2023), Tsipras et al. (2019), and Ilyas et al. (2019) discussions and references. Related work emphasizes joint attack/defense scaling more directly, while retaining the study's central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and parts of the results discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting and reorganization. The five findings become a numbered list, and Author Contributions and Impact Statement sections are added. These are extensive editorial changes despite largely retained appendix prose.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column report to a two-column conference layout with different typography and headers. Figure 3 expands to include existing BEAST results, new main-text Figure 5 presents the previously appended efficiency analysis, and Figure 2 gains Qwen2.5 curves and legend entries. The visual changes extend well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The additional Qwen2.5 tests check the central size–robustness finding on two more existing tasks, reducing reliance on Spam and Harmless for that family. The code link and more prominent efficiency evidence improve reproducibility information and accessibility. These are limited gains: most scientific content remains unchanged, some curve revisions are unexplained, and the newly flagged RandomToken compute-axis error remains uncorrected.
